dockets.summary: Every notifier-facing string says Great Britain and no address is checked by nation; the England-only drafting of the draft SI is parked as a legal note that changes no page. Plants and wood answer a Yes/No arrival-status question (never derived from the date) before giving one date — expected landing or first arrival — and a destination that is the intended destination or, once the consignment is there, its current location; potatoes give an expected date and time and are never asked whether they have arrived. The arrival date is validated only as a real calendar date with one sourced bound (a consignment that has already arrived cannot have a future date) and no typo window; lateness is never validation. Lateness is computed in calendar days by one pure helper (potatoes late after arrivalDate minus 2, plants and wood late after arrivalDate plus 4, time ignored), shown live as a warning on the draft check-your-answers page, committed as a system value at the first submission (reconciled to D5's model) and read back for the banner on confirmation and the submitted view and the Late tag on the dashboard — all buildable now with no engine change — while routing to APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government is parked as backend work.

The contact section collapses to the single animals-shaped address-book pick: the picked record already carries the contact's name, address, telephone and email (the address book will not store a record without the last two), so the plants-only number-and-email page and its two obligations are deleted and Check your answers shows all four from the copied record. Consignment Number stays an optional notifier reference because no source defines it, and its definition is parked. The consignor is picked from the address book as animals does but is asked only for plants for planting and wood — the potato regulation lists no consignor, and the reconciler's 'oversight' reading is a policy answer nobody has — with a typed fallback for EU consignors parked. The country-of-origin error sentence swaps 'the animal' for 'the consignment' and the obligation becomes an honest variant; the declaration keeps every animals mechanism but replaces the five animals statements with three short plants statements grounded in the policy paper, with the third-party authority clauses parked alongside agents (standing ruling 2). Nothing in this docket needs Sam.

The commodity model stands as the reconciler drafted it: one notification-level type (potatoes, plants for planting, wood and cut trees), nine per-line categories taken straight from the SI's scope items, one-or-many commodity lines, a fifteen-entry genus list served as reference data with hardwood lines narrowed to Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus, species as free text, and seed potatoes treated as potatoes. Every wood and potato scope condition (bark, origin, the 3-metre threshold, preservative treatment, the Balearic Islands) is guidance on the page rather than a question, with the preservative note moved to the category question and given its cut-trees exception, and the Balearic and four-country note shown as an inset on the origin page only when a ware-potato line exists. Wipe wins over retain everywhere, and a change of commodity type after lines exist now drops the incompatible lines in the commodity-type POST itself (warning before, banner after), not on the list page's load, so stale lines can never reach the hub, check your answers or submission. Nothing needs Sam: the two genuinely open points (whether conifer wood lines owe a genus, and which plants for planting are legally trees) are parked as policy checks, and the trees-for-planting category value is built now so the size-of-tree matter can be asked.

Every item in this docket is out of the first pass and stays that way: the four conflicts resolve to the readings the spec already carries (proceed on the two Confluence pages as read; the signed-in Defra ID organisation is the notifier; Defra ID sign-in is the only precondition; many commodity lines in one notification is the commodityLines collection), and all thirteen behaviours are parked, not rejected. Nothing new is built: no agent or importer party, no registration step, no bulk upload or document import, no regulator, inspector or analyst screens, no list-maintenance admin, no check booking, no documents collection, no outbox or event publishing, no combined animals+plants list. Five small spec edits keep the record honest: the declaration page records that no third-party or authority sentence survives (c-028, standing ruling 2), reuse-a-previous-consignment stays parked because c-030 ruled Copy as new out with the prototype templates pattern closed off, the regulator-views detail stops claiming a region is captured, the outbox behaviour records that the eventual mapper must carry every SI matter, and the combined-list behaviour records the two-dashboards cost for a trader who imports both. Nothing needs Sam; the users/agents/registration items and bulk upload are attributed to his standing rulings, the rest to the panel.

This docket settles what the origin page and the free-text fields may check. Country of origin stays one field over the animals country list (which already holds every country the law names), and the law's own scope lists are enforced when the notifier presses Continue: ware potatoes must come from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain, conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain, and other plants and wood from an EU member state; the Balearic Islands exclusion is the origin-page inset ruled at D2, and Check your answers re-checks the rule so a line added later cannot leave a stale origin. Every field no source formats stays free text with a length cap; the only checks added are a real-time rule for the potato arrival time and a corrected quantity hint (the contact email and number go with D4's contact ruling), and the optional 'use' field for plants and wood is dropped because the draft SI does not list it. The ports endpoint turns out to be built, so the place of landing uses it now; confirming whether plants keeps the animals country block is the one item left for Sam, and it blocks nothing.

The reference number, status and submission model stay exactly as animals built them: the frontend prints whatever the backend mints, the status is the four-value lifecycle with lateness shown as a separate Late tag and banner, and the confirmation page only appears once the backend has stored the submitted record with its own timestamp. The plants type-code prefix is parked until someone supplies it, and its Sam-gated backend change moves to the end of the backlog so it no longer blocks the confirmation page and the end-to-end tests. Post-submission Amend, Cancel amendment and Delete are built as in animals (policy is silent, the engine and backend already support them, and delete is a soft delete so the regulator's record survives); Copy as new stays parked with the reuse-a-previous-consignment need the brief excludes. The late flag is fixed at the first submission and does not move when a notification is amended; whether it should, and whether a submitted notification may be withdrawn once the regulator has acted, are recorded as open policy questions rather than blockers, so nothing in this docket needs Sam to rule today.

The plants journey keeps the animals chrome exactly as it is (service name Import notification service, Alpha banner and its feedback address, the two placeholder links) and the confirmation page tells the trader to contact the relevant plant health authority — APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government — with no invented helpdesk; the plants-specific naming, feedback and support decisions stay on the Sam-gated chore, but the English-only unauthorised view and two stack-hygiene items come off that gate and build now. The dashboard is a plants-only list of this session's notifications with no cross-journey filter, and the journey has the full animals shape: an opening run in section order, a grouped task-list hub, section captions and a flow-only declaration — with one correction, that the commodity entry sub-page is not a run step, and a build-order rule that each section adds its own hub row. Guidance stays on GOV.UK (the dashboard intro links to it only when a real URL exists and the commodity-type hints quote the SI timing windows verbatim), the pre-2021 scheme and NI/RoI precedents are parked as copy inputs, and the volatility of the commodity list and timing windows becomes a standing build constraint: lists as data behind the set-owned commodities service, each window one named constant, territory and authority names as copy leaves. Nothing in this docket needs Sam.

The ten Annex 6 non-functional and management-information items split cleanly: five are adopted because the engine already delivers the journey's share (page-level accessibility, GDS Design System conformance, 24x7 readiness, minimal trader effort, the coded values and timestamps that feed the eight metrics), and five are parked because the policy paper gives no answer (GDPR lawful basis and retention, the meaning of 'sustainable', a live Welsh service) or because Sam has ruled users and internal access out of this phase (internal login, cross-organisation access parity). Two verified corrections come out of the adoption: the axe tag list is widened so the WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run, and a new two-repo fix extra carries submittedAt onto the backend's notifications list so the dashboard's Date submitted row stops rendering empty in real mode. The footer's Privacy and Accessibility statement links both point at generic GOV.UK pages and are routed through the existing Sam-gated chrome extra. Nothing needs Sam's decision now; the countryOfOrigin 'animal' error copy that one judge flagged is already conflict c-027 and is left to its own docket.

rulings.resolution: 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrivalDate labels by state, proposedPlaceOfLanding hint, confirmation body; the dashboard intro names no territory today — guidance-before-you-start) and the service applies no nation or territory check to the placeOfDestination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service. The SI's England-only drafting is recorded as a legal note on the england-vs-great-britain behaviour, not rendered and not built.
rulings.rationale: Outside the SI's operative clauses the policy paper is GB throughout: section:policy/para:2 ('into GB'), para:6/item:1-2 ('arrival in GB'), para:7 (APHA, FC or Scottish Government spot-check at destination), section:summary/para:4 (all three need access), annex:6/functional/item:11 (SG and FC get the same access as APHA); and the SI's own destination clause reg 26(2)(b) says 'intended destination in Great Britain' — a consignment landing in England may be bound for Scotland or Wales and is still notified. The tier-2 sources are unanimous: every NNS-UN Applies-to cell is 'EU > GB', the mural service card is 'High risk Plants EU -> GB', and both the Confluence requirements page (h4:All other goods/li:1) and the mural data-fields board (file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:1) transcribe reg 26(2)(a) itself as 'landing in GB ... arrived in Great Britain' (verified in the extracts). No source asks the notifier to state or prove the nation of arrival, so a territorial check would invent an obligation; either string is feature copy, so the engine imposes nothing. The spec already carries Great Britain on arrivalStatus.label, the arrival-status page title, arrivalDate.input.labelByState and proposedPlaceOfLanding.hint; the one thing it does not yet say is that the destination address is not territorially checked.

rulings.resolution: Collect exactly the statutory matters: one arrivalDate for every commodity type; arrivalTime only when commodityType = potatoes; arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees. A potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival ('Expected date of arrival'), a past date is accepted and flagged late by lateNotificationIndicator, never rejected, and no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes; the arrival-status page needs no authored gate because the derived gate hides it for potatoes.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(2)(a) 'the expected time and date of their arrival' is the only potato timing matter and reg 24A has no post-arrival branch; reg 26(2)(a) branches ('or, if the consignment has arrived in England, the date on which it first arrived') and has no time. h4:Potatoes (seed and ware)/li:1, h4:All other goods/li:1, file:data-fields/region:Potatoes/item:1 and region:Other goods/item:1 restate the same split, so there is nothing to adjudicate — only a gap for late potatoes, which file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2 proves exist and section:non-compliance/para:2 treats as a non-compliance to manage, not a reason to refuse. Inventing a potato already-arrived matter would add a question no source asks (NNS-UN-010 proportionate; Article 9(7) OCR strictly-necessary, section:legal-basis/para:1). NNS-UN-035 (one date field whose meaning switches) is met by arrivalDate.labelByState. Engine: both gates are top-level scalar gates on commodityType (equalsGate for arrivalTime, includesGate for arrivalStatus), same frame, wipeOnExit by the evaluator; the arrival-status page collects only arrivalStatus so pageGatePasses fails for potatoes by the derived rule (skeleton derived-gates) — the spec's page.gate currently holds a prose string an implementor may read as an authored gate, and should be null. The one service-design gap is the label 'Expected date of arrival' shown to somebody whose potatoes arrived yesterday: a hint line resolves it without a new matter.

rulings.resolution: The importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question page (plants and wood only, radios Yes first) before arrival-details and place-of-destination; the service never derives it from the date. Because the SI's two either/ors are not the same condition — the date turns on 'arrived in England', the location on 'arrived at its intended destination' — the destination page's already-arrived copy tells a notifier whose consignment has landed but not reached its destination to give the intended destination, so one binary status serves both clauses.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(a)-(b) frame arrival as a fact the operator states ('if the consignment has arrived'), and NNS-UN-036 ('based on the current status of my consignment'), NNS-UN-001 and NNS-UN-025 ('pre-nots'/'post-nots') treat it as something the importer knows; NNS-UN-010 is met because it is a single radio, not a data matter. Deriving from arrivalDate is wrong on the day of arrival and for an expected date that has slipped, and would make the destination page's copy depend on a clock read rather than an answer — which the model cannot express and the copy tripwires cannot pin; one-thing-per-page favours a discrete radios page, and the derived gate hides it for potatoes at no cost. Reg 26(2)(b)'s condition is 'arrived at its intended destination in Great Britain', so a consignment that has landed and is in transit must give the intended destination — 'Where is the consignment now?' alone would mislead — and a hint covers it without a third state. Yes first: animals' own yes/no radios read 'Yes | No' (live-animals extract, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement and containsUnweanedAnimals) and the GOV.UK Design System's yes/no examples lead with Yes; an order-only edit with no model change. The spec already matches the pick otherwise.

rulings.resolution: arrivalDate validates as a real calendar date (dateText) with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds; the single bound is sourced — when arrivalStatus = already-arrived the date may not be after today in Europe/London (dateTextInRange, max only) because it is 'the date on which it first arrived' — and the picker carries data-max-date only in that state and no data-min-date in any state. Expected dates (potatoes, not-yet-arrived) accept any past or future date; lateness is computed, never validated; a typo sanity window is parked, not built.
rulings.rationale: No plants source bounds the date: the timing rules are relative to it (section:policy/para:6; annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)), annex:6/functional/item:2 and section:non-compliance/para:2 require a late notification to be accepted, and file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2 needs a past date. Animals' [today - 7 days, today + 6 months] (live-animals arrivalDateAtPort validationRaw; arrival.js:5) would reject the mural late-potato fixture whenever the lorry arrived more than a week ago — a plants-source reason to diverge under standing ruling 5. The already-arrived ceiling is the SI's own semantics (reg 26(2)(a)) and stops a self-contradictory answer (already arrived, future date) that would also make the lateness rule nonsense; it can never refuse a lawful notification because a consignment that has arrived has arrived today or earlier. A one-year-each-way sanity window has no source — its numbers would be a policy answer nobody has (standing ruling 1) — and a picker min/max would display a rule the regulation does not impose; it is parked. Engine: dateTextInRange takes optional min and max (lib/validate/validators.js:269-271 — verified, max alone works), the bounds helper beside arrival-details returns { max, maxText } from one clock read (skeleton date-fields; docs/validation.md), and the controller builds the schema in POST from answers.arrivalStatus as it already does for scope.has() fields. No model change.

rulings.resolution: The SI wording wins: plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival; potatoes only before, at least two days before the expected date. Lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London and ignores arrivalTime — potatoes are late when the notification day is after arrivalDate minus 2 days, plants and wood when it is after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on arrivalDate minus 2, or on arrivalDate plus 4, is on time); a future date can still be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood, and the windows are shown up front as option hints on commodity-type and per state on arrival-status.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1) 'before or no later than four days after the date of their arrival' is the only text that explicitly admits a pre-arrival plants notification and reg 26(2)(a) presupposes it; section:policy/para:6/item:2 is a shorter restatement of the same rule, not a contradiction, and standing ruling 4 gives the SI precedence in any case. Reg 24A(1) 'at least two days before the expected date of their arrival' counts by date, so the unit is the calendar day and the potato time (reg 24A(2)(a)) is a matter to record, not part of the deadline — recorded as a provisional reading. NNS-UN-001/025/036's generic pre/post vocabulary is consistent with the split and supplies no commodity rule of its own. The spec is inconsistent with itself: the commodity-type page notes and the adopted guidance-link-not-in-journey-pages behaviour promise per-option timing hints but commodityType carries no valueHints (verified). The calendar helpers startOfDayInZone, startOfUtcDay and addUtcDays exist in lib/validate/calendar.js (verified), so the rule is a pure function with no new library code.

rulings.resolution: After submission the late highlight is shown in three places — a govukNotificationBanner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the SUBMITTED read-only check-your-answers view, and a Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card; before submission the DRAFT check-your-answers page shows govukWarningText when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, computed by the same helper with the request clock, and says it can still be submitted. It never blocks and there is no separate late page. lateNotificationIndicator is a manifest obligation with system: true, listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED: one pure helper computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) and is called twice — with the request clock for the DRAFT check-your-answers warning, and with the finalise clock in the declaration POST, whose result is committed as a system value in fulfilment immediately before submitJourney only when the journey is DRAFT (c-030); confirmation, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt.
rulings.rationale: annex:6/functional/item:2 'Highlight to the user (internal and external) when a notification was made outside of required timings' is past tense and names both audiences: the confirmation banner and read-only CYA serve the notifier and the stored submittedAt plus answers serve the regulator (NNS-UN-014); NNS-UN-012 wants the rule named, not just 'late'; section:non-compliance/para:2 lists late notification among non-compliances managed by advice, warnings or sanctions, so submission proceeds. No source asks for a pre-submission warning and the policy judge saw a trade-off; the panel builds it because NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is correct, avoid errors) and NNS-UN-012 ('so that I can meet the rules') are both served by telling the notifier before they commit, a mistyped date is exactly what CYA exists to catch, the commodity-type hints already name the rule so the warning reveals nothing new, the Design System's warning text exists for something the user needs to know before continuing, and the engineering judge showed it is the same pure helper with a different clock argument — one component on an existing page, no engine change. Engine: submitJourney is records.finalise and nothing else (engine/write/submit.js — verified) and checks only recognised keys and readiness, so the declaration controller commits the helper's result as a system value before calling it and a system value no page collects never blocks; the backend and the stub re-stamp submittedAt on every submission and keep no first-submission timestamp (stub/lifecycle/transition.js:14, :32, :47; NotificationAggregate.submittedAt), which is why the flag is stored at the first finalise from DRAFT rather than derived from submittedAt (c-030 — Amend is in scope); the boot guard requires a system obligation to be listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED (boot-guards-three); the mapper has no typed home (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/limits.md), so the flag travels in the opaque fulfilments payload with an explicit omission assertion on the NotificationDto. No finalise hook and no engine change.

rulings.resolution: Build it in the first pass as a stored system value: a pure lateness helper beside the check-answers feature computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) using the c-031 calendar-day rule; the declaration POST calls it with the finalise clock and commits the result as the lateNotificationIndicator system value (manifest obligation, system: true, in SYSTEM_POPULATED) immediately before submitJourney when the journey is DRAFT, leaving it untouched on a re-submit from AMEND (c-030); the draft CYA calls the same helper with the request clock for its warning; confirmation, the submitted CYA and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value (c-035). No finalise hook, no backend field, no engine change.
rulings.rationale: Sourced by section:policy/para:6/item:1-2, annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1), annex:6/functional/item:2, NNS-UN-012 and NNS-UN-014. rulings.resolution: The SI wins on scope: the consignor is required for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees only and is never asked for potatoes — the potato list traces the crop through producer and crop identification numbers instead. rulings.rationale: Reg 26(2)(f) 'the name and address of the consignor' sits in the plants-and-wood matters; reg 24A(2) lists eight potato matters and no consignor (verified at .sources/phnns-policy.txt lines 274-321). Annex 2 and Annex 6 repeat the split, and the policy team's two restatements agree (extract.confluence-requirements consignor under h4:All other goods/li:7 with the potato list carrying none; extract.mural consignorNameAndAddress under file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:7 only). Four concordant sources are not an oversight — potatoes are traced through the producer identification number and crop identification number (reg 24A(2)(e)-(f)), which plants and wood do not have — so reading the omission as a drafting slip is a policy answer nobody has, which standing ruling 1 parks and standing ruling 4 (the SI is the authority on WHAT is collected) forbids the panel to overrule; Article 9(7) OCR 'strictly necessary' (section:legal-basis/para:1) and NNS-UN-004/NNS-UN-010 point the same way. The gate is buildable today: activatedBy { obligation: commodityType, includes: [...] } with wipeOnExit is the same-frame shape the spec already uses on arrivalStatus (skeleton helper vocabulary: includesGate on a top-level scalar), the derived page gate hides consignor-select and the row status rules mark the row NA (hub-task-list-and-row-status). rulings.resolution: Keep the declaration page and its machinery exactly as animals has them — the single checkbox, its confirmation sentence in English and Welsh, the error copy, the date line, Continue, the flow-only key and submit gate. Replace the five animals statements wholesale: none survives. The first pass carries three short plants statements grounded in the policy paper — (1) this submission is the written notification to the competent authority under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme; (2) the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may spot-check the consignment without prior notice at its place of destination or where it is currently held; (3) failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance — flagged provisional copy for policy and content-design sign-off, with no Welsh invented. The third-party / agent-authority clauses are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2, not written, and every spec line saying the plants declaration 'carries the third-party clause' is corrected. The sub-park of the third-party and agent-authority clauses is decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2).
rulings.rationale: No plants source prescribes declaration wording: the SI requires only 'written notification to the competent authority' by the professional operator (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)); the paper, both Confluence pages and the mural are silent; the prototype has a declaration checkbox and submit with no statements (extract.prototype declaration route). The engine already supports the shape (skeleton flow-only-keys-declaration; adopted declaration-and-submit-gate), so the checkbox, sentence and semantics are a same-as-animals first-pass build. The truth-and-accuracy checkbox is grounded — 'Incorrect notification details' is a named non-compliance (section:non-compliance/para:2/item:2) and NNS-UN-007 wants confidence the notification is complete and correct — so the animals sentence stands verbatim. Each animals statement (repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend .../features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js) fails a plants source: 'cleared border control checks' contradicts the premise that border controls are removed (section:policy/para:1-2; customs-no-sps-hold-or-matching); 'payments for border control checks' contradicts the no-fees decision (section:fees-and-charges/para:1; no-fees-no-payment-step); 'quarantine or isolation of the animals' is on the live-animals extract's LIVE-ANIMALS-SPECIFIC COPY list; 're-dispatch', 'destruction and disposal' and 'contact for the authorities and located in the UK' have no plants source. The two clauses on acting for a third party assert a delegation model that standing ruling 2 puts out of this phase — they are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf (NNS-UN-039) — and the GDS judge's 'I am the professional operator ... or I am authorised to make this notification on their behalf' would also decide c-038 (who notifies) by the back door. The three replacement statements restate facts the paper already asserts rather than imposing new undertakings: written-notification-attributable (reg 24A(1)/26(1)); random spot checks at destination by APHA, FC or Scottish Government (section:policy/para:7) without prior notice (section:legal-basis/para:3/item:4; checks-without-prior-notice-no-booking-step), with 'where it is currently held' covering the already-arrived branch (reg 26(2)(b)); and the paper's three non-compliance examples in full (section:non-compliance/para:2 — failure to notify, incorrect details, late) rather than late alone (late-accepted-not-rejected). They are provisional copy pending policy sign-off; Welsh is not invented (brief).

rulings.resolution: Seed potatoes are potatoes: commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters (variety, quantity, intended use, producer and crop ids, time of arrival, place of landing) and the two-day pre-arrival window. The mural list-image's placement of seed potatoes under Plants for planting is not followed and 'Seed potatoes' is never a genus value.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1)(a) names seed potatoes as the first class of potatoes and reg 24A(1)(b) defines ware as 'potatoes, other than seed potatoes', so seed potatoes carry the reg 24A(2) matters and the 'at least two days before' timing. Annex 1 lists 'Seed potatoes' as its own item beside 'Ware potatoes', not under plants for planting; the mural data-fields board (file:data-fields/region:Potatoes (ware and seed)) and the Confluence page (h4:Potatoes (seed and ware)) agree. Only mural list-image row 16 dissents and its own note (seed-potatoes-listed-under-plants-for-planting) says the board does not resolve it; standing ruling 4 puts the policy paper first. The two category values are needed because the origin scope differs (seed: any part of the Common SPS Area bar the UK, Channel Islands and Isle of Man; ware: Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain). The spec already carries this on commodityType.input.values, category.input.valuesByCommodityType.potatoes, potatoVariety/potatoIntendedUse gated on the two potato categories, arrivalTime gated on commodityType = potatoes, and genus.input.valuesNote ('seed potatoes are not a genus'). All three judges agree.

rulings.resolution: The SI wording wins: the category value is conifer-wood-with-bark, labelled 'Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer'. The mural table's 'with mark' is a transcription typo and carries no meaning.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i) reads 'conifer wood with bark and isolated bark of conifer from a member State, excluding preservative-treated wood'. The mural extract's own transcription-drift note records that the embedded OFFSEN image (file:list-image/row:18) reads 'bark' and only the Mural-native re-typed table (file:list-table/row:18) reads 'mark'; both mural forms truncate the SI item anyway. Tier one over tier two under standing ruling 4. The spec's category.input.valueLabels already carries the SI reading; the label stays provisional for the copy pass and needs Welsh before release (nfr-english-and-welsh). All three judges agree.

rulings.resolution: The four wood caveats are scope conditions, not data elements: they become the five wood category values (with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in the value labels) and guidance copy; the only extra wood data collected is the two SI matters, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments, gated same-frame on category. No question is asked about preservative treatment, bark condition or the 3-metre threshold. The preservative exclusion moves from the treatments hint to a hint on the category question shown for wood notifications, worded with its cut-coniferous-trees exception.
rulings.rationale: The SI separates scope from matters: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i)-(iv) says who must notify (bark, origin, preservative exclusion, height, form) and reg 26(2)(h)-(i) are the only wood matters. Article 9(7) OCR limits notification data to what is 'strictly necessary' (section:legal-basis/para:1), so a preservative or height question would collect a datum the SI does not list; a consignment outside reg 26(1)(b) attracts no duty. The mural author offers the caveats 'in case you need this level of detail' (file:data-fields/region:Wood/preamble, note wood-caveats-are-scope-detail) and the Confluence extractor flagged the heading as ambiguous rather than as a data claim. Engine: category is a within-member gate so allowListed(category, values, null) scopes sizeOfTree and phytosanitaryTreatments per line with no modelGap (add-a-collection.md section 2). Two corrections to the spec as drafted. First, the scope condition must be visible at the moment of choosing (NNS-UN-013 wood importer, NNS-UN-010 proportionate), not only in the treatments hint the trader sees after committing to a wood category. Second, the current treatments hint 'Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified' is gated on all five wood categories including cut-coniferous-trees, yet reg 26(1)(b)(iii) carries no preservative exclusion, so on a cut-trees line that sentence is wrong; a single wood-level hint on the category question with the exception stated says it once and correctly. Per-option hints repeating the four-country and 3-metre conditions are not added because the value labels already carry them.

rulings.resolution: '(for plants for planting)' qualifies species only. Genus is asked for plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, hardwood-round-surface and hardwood-chips lines; species only for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting; the three conifer lines (conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees) ask neither in the first pass. The literal reading that reg 26(2)(c) also wants a genus for conifer wood is recorded on the obligation as a parked policy check, not built.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(c) reads 'the category (e.g. plants for planting or cut wood), genus, species (for plants for planting) and commodity code'; the bracket sits immediately after species, and where the SI qualifies a whole matter it leads with 'in the case of' (reg 26(2)(g)-(i)), so species is plants-for-planting only. Genus for hardwood lines is a statutorily listed value (reg 26(1)(b)(iv) 'wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus') and is offered. For conifer wood the scope items say only 'conifer' and no source supplies a conifer genus list, so a conifer genus control cannot be populated today (standing ruling 1); a free-text genus with no list and no validation runs against Annex 6 'Standardise information' and 'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8-9) and is impractical for isolated bark and mixed chips. The policy judge's claim that Annex 3 reaches for conifer genus does not survive reading it: Annex 3's Wood products section groups pests under 'Cut coniferous trees>3m', 'Conifer wood with bark and all isolated conifer bark' and 'Conifer wood without bark' (Ips, Bursaphelenchus, Fusarium by bark condition and form), and names a genus only for hardwood ('Wood of ash', 'Wood of Castanea', 'Wood of Platanus') — which is exactly the split the spec makes. Confluence (h4:All other goods/li:3 with its qualifier note) and the mural (file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:3) carry the same sentence and cannot tip it. The spec's genus.activatedBy.includes and species.activatedBy.includes already encode this; the note makes the omission deliberate and revisitable when policy answers.

rulings.resolution: The hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service; the mural and Confluence lists that still carry them (and the mural spelling 'Juglens') are superseded by the SI footnotes.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(iv) lists 'wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus' and footnotes 2 and 3 (policy extract juglans-pterocarya-removed-from-scope, provenance footnote:2, alsoStatedAt footnote:3) say Juglans and Pterocarya 'were included in the original scope but have now been removed as they are no longer considered to be hosts of Agrilus planipennis'. The mural (file:list-image/row:22, 'Juglens') and the Confluence caveats (h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:4) predate that removal and are tier two under standing ruling 4. Offering an out-of-scope genus would invite notifications the scheme does not require (NNS-UN-010). The spec's genus.input.valuesByCategory already reads Castanea, Fraxinus, Platanus for both hardwood categories; the list lives in the set-owned commodities service checked by whitelists.test.js (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2, annex:1 closing paragraph), so a future reinstatement is a data change. rulings.resolution: A notification carries one or many commodity lines: commodityLines is a collection with minEntries 1 (error 'Add at least one commodity'), built as the two-page batch (list page plus Commodity details entry sub-page) as a variant of animals' commodityLines without its catalogue search. All lines share the one commodityType chosen first; a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications. Bulk upload of many notifications is a separate matter already parked under c-040.
rulings.rationale: The SI's singular 'the consignment' (annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)-(d), reg:24A(2)(d)) describes the movement, not a cap on its contents: a consignment of two genera or several potato varieties can only meet 'genus, species ... commodity code' and 'their variety and quantity' by reporting each. NNS-UN-005 ('large shipments efficiently ... high volumes of consignments') and NNS-UN-006 ('detailed and flexible product information') push toward many lines; the mural's 59k notifications a year (file:blueprint/left header card) is volume, not lines. The reg 24A / reg 26 split (different matters, different windows) justifies one commodityType per notification (one-notification-per-commodity-type, adopted). Engine: collections are first-class (skeleton collections-engine-api; add-a-collection.md section 1 requires.minEntries) and collections-two-page-batch is adopted; animals' commodityLines is the consistency anchor (standing ruling 5) with the divergence recorded on the obligation. The spec already says all of this. All three judges agree.

rulings.resolution: Wipe wins: wipeOnExit = true stays on every gated plants obligation and no answer is retained out of scope. A change of commodityType after lines exist is handled in the commodity-type page's POST, not on the list page's load: the page warns before the change when lines exist, the POST commits the type and then drops the lines whose category is not in the new type's set via reconcileEntriesAt, and redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner names what was removed; the list page suppresses its zero-lines redirect for that load and never writes on GET.
rulings.rationale: No plants source asks for retention: NNS-UN-041 is about reusing a previous consignment (reuse-previous-consignment, parked) and NNS-UN-006's 'flexible' is coloured red, meaning unstated. Policy points to wipe: Annex 6 'Standardise information' and 'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8-9), Article 9(7) strictly-necessary (section:legal-basis/para:1), and 'Incorrect notification details' as a named non-compliance (section:non-compliance list) — a wood notification still carrying a potato variety is exactly that. The engine's Yes-No-Yes rule is the default (docs/scope-and-wipe.md: 'when a controlling answer makes a value leave scope, the value is deleted. Returning to the earlier branch does not restore stale data') and animals' only retain is regionOfOriginCode, so wipe also keeps consistency under standing ruling 5. For the lines, category is always in scope on the line and 'a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition' (skeleton helper-selection-rule), so the model cannot drop them; but reconcileEntriesAt exists (engine/write/entries/reconcile.js, exported from engine/index.js) and keys existing entries, keeps those still present and drops the rest with wipe semantics, and animals reconciles commodityLines by lineKey on the save that changes the selection (live-animals extract, commodities search page). The reconciler's provisional pick — reconcile on the list page's load — fails twice: add-a-collection.md forbids a GET triggering a delete ('no GET can trigger a delete'), and a trader who changes type from a CYA Change link is returned to CYA by kit.exitTarget (skeleton change context) without visiting the list, leaving stale lines counted complete by the hub, CYA and submit. Doing it in the POST that changes the controlling answer closes the hole at the moment it opens. The count travels on the redirect query string because that is the engine's own post-redirect convention (shared/kit.js:177 sets ?staleAction=1); the engine judge's 'no yar' claim is wrong (yar backs the session cache) but the precedent stands. Because the nine categories partition by type, kept is empty whenever the type really changes, which is why the warning text before the change is worth its one line. One hole the judges missed: the commodities list page redirects to the entry sub-page whenever it has zero lines (page shape, copied from animals emptyRedirect inverted), so a ?removed load must render rather than redirect or the banner is never seen. Three typed collections (three groups, duplicated quantity/genus/commodityCode/use, three CYA cards) and retain-and-flag (an unsubmittable notification the trader cannot fix from CYA) are not built.

rulings.resolution: The genus list for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting lines is the fifteen entries of reg 26(1)(a) with the SI's spelling and bracketed English names; the four species-level entries are offered as they stand; 'Seed potatoes' is not a genus; hardwood lines get the same control rendered with Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. The list is set-owned reference data, not a hard-coded enum, and the details page offers only the entries allowed for the line's category — never fifteen with twelve rejected.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(a)(i)-(xv) is the statutory list and tier one ('Polygala myrtifolia (myrtle-leaf milkwort)', 'Salvia rosmarinus (rosemary)'); Annex 1 holds the same fifteen regrouped as ten plus five Xylella shrub hosts, so there is no drift inside the policy paper. The mural's sixteenth row is seed potatoes, ruled a potato under c-004, and its 'Salvia Rosmarinus' and 'myrtle leaved milkwort' are tier-two transcription variants (file:list-image/rows:1-16). The Confluence page gives no list. Annex 6 wants 'easy maintenance of ... Genus & species in scope' (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2) and Annex 1's closing paragraph says the list 'will be dynamic', which the set-owned commodities service and whitelists.test.js satisfy (set-owned-commodities-service, restore-whitelists-test). The bracketed common names keep the control plain English for a trader who knows 'oak' not 'Quercus'. Because commodity-details is server-rendered on POST after category is chosen (page shape), the option list itself can be the per-category list; the spec's 'narrowed by page-side validation' alone reads as fifteen rendered and twelve rejected, which the GOV.UK error pattern discourages, so the note is tightened.

rulings.rationale: The three types are the SI's own partition — reg 24A (potatoes), reg 26(1)(a) (plants for planting), reg 26(1)(b) (wood and cut trees) — with different matters and timing windows, matching the mural's data-fields regions and Annex 1's headings. The SI only exemplifies category ('e.g. plants for planting or cut wood', annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)), so the value list is derived from the scope items themselves: reg 24A(1)(a)/(b), reg 26(1)(a) split by c-019, reg 26(1)(b)(i), (ii), (iii), (iv)(aa), (iv)(bb); every value is traceable to a statutory item and each carries distinct scope conditions and gated matters. Collapsing to the mural's Plants for planting / Ware potatoes / Bark / Wood / Cut Trees (file:list-image/column:1) would lose the bark-by-origin and round-surface/chips distinctions the SI needs (c-037) and the potato split (c-004). All three judges agree.

rulings.resolution: Keep 'trees for planting' as a per-line category value beside 'plants for planting' so the notifier declares that the plants are trees and sizeOfTree gates same-frame on category in [trees-for-planting, cut-coniferous-trees]. Both options get a neutral hint that lets the trader self-classify without policy knowledge; the genus list is not narrowed for trees for planting. Which plants-for-planting lines legally count as trees is a parked policy question, and the genus-derived alternative is not built.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(h) requires 'in the case of cut trees or trees for planting, the size of the tree' but reg 26(1) defines no 'trees for planting' class: plants for planting are scoped by genus and only cut coniferous trees by height (reg 26(1)(b)(iii)). Annex 1's split is the only hint and it is never labelled 'trees' — Olea europaea sits in the first group while Annex 3 lists it as a Xylella host, and Prunus is grown as a shrub — so reading the first group as a legal tree list would invent a classification. The notifier already has to know whether the plants are trees to know whether the SI requires size, so asking them to say so makes the statutory condition answerable without inventing an obligation; asking size of every plants-for-planting line would over-collect against Article 9(7) and NNS-UN-010. Engine: 'genus in tree genera OR category = cut-coniferous-trees' is two conditions on one obligation, which the helper vocabulary does not offer (skeleton helper-selection-rule; a gate reads one gate value), and the only expressible genus-driven form is two size obligations, splitting one statutory matter into two CYA rows against c-015; under standing ruling 1 the category value is what is built now. The residual design risk is a trader not knowing whether their Quercus whips are 'trees', so the two options carry hints; the copy is invented and provisional.

rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(c) requires 'species (for plants for planting)' and gives no list; the statutory scope is genus-level except for those four entries (reg 26(1)(a)(vi), (vii), (xi), (xiv)). Annex 6's 'easy maintenance of ... Genus & species in scope' (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2) describes a future catalogue no source supplies, so a coded species control would be invented (standing ruling 1); 'Standardise information' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8) is met at genus level where a list exists. rulings.resolution: The SI's two items win: conifer-wood-with-bark ('Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer', any member State) and conifer-wood-without-bark ('Conifer wood without bark', Italy, France, Portugal and Spain only), with the four-country origin constraint on the second value alone. The Confluence and mural rephrasing is not modelled as a third value.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i) 'conifer wood with bark and isolated bark of conifer from a member State' and (ii) 'conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain'. The tier-two restatement 'with or without bark ... from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain' (h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:2; file:data-fields/region:Wood/bullet:2) folds with-bark wood from those four countries into (ii), which (i) already covers from any member State — the same practical scope, but its wording would put an origin constraint on with-bark wood that the SI does not impose; standing ruling 4 takes the SI. Annex 3 confirms the split is deliberate (Bursaphelenchus xylophilus 'from France, Portugal, Spain' listed under 'Conifer wood without bark'). Two values keep the origin narrowing a per-category allow-list (countryOfOrigin.input.valueConstraints conifer-wood-without-bark = [IT, FR, PT, ES]) and the category label names the four countries so the trader can self-select before the origin page (commodity precedes origin, c-022). Whether an out-of-scope origin is rejected or accepted is origin-value-list-by-commodity, not on this docket. All three judges agree.

rulings.resolution: Build it in the first pass exactly as ruled in c-013: the commodity-type POST, after committing a changed commodityType, reconciles commodityLines with reconcileEntriesAt (keep lines whose category is in the new type's set, drop the rest with wipe semantics), the page warns before when lines exist, and it redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner reports the removal and the zero-lines redirect is suppressed for that load. The on-load reconcile, three typed collections and retain-and-flag alternatives are not built; a model-owned projection helper is recorded as a candidate extension.
rulings.rationale: The engine already exposes reconcileEntriesAt with wipe semantics (engine/write/entries/reconcile.js keeps entries still present by key and drops the rest; skeleton collections-engine-api) and animals reconciles by key on the save that changes the controlling selection (live-animals commodities search page), so the increment is one branch in the commodity-type POST, one banner on the list page, and tests in controller.test.js — cheap and consistent under standing ruling 5. The model cannot own it because a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition (skeleton helper-selection-rule) and per-instance scope wipes fields, not instances (skeleton scope-and-wipe). Reconciling on list-page load would write on GET, which add-a-collection.md forbids for deletes, or leave a wood notification carrying a seed-potato line that the hub, CYA and submit count complete until the page is revisited — a hole a CYA Change link on commodity-type opens directly. Three typed collections would triple the collection pages and duplicate quantity against NNS-UN-004 and the one-obligation-per-concept reading in c-015; retain-and-flag leaves an unsubmittable notification. The e2e-commodity-section extra already names 'changing commodity type drops incompatible lines'.

rulings.resolution: The SI wins: the notifier is the professional operator bringing the goods into England, and in this service that is the signed-in Defra ID organisation. The journey collects no importer, agent or notifier party; the consignor (reg 26(2)(f)) is the only party obligation. The declaration carries no third-party, standing, authority or agent sentence — both animals third-party statements are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2 (c-028) — and its statement bullets are the three plants statements ruled at c-028. Agent identification, authorisation and linking stay parked under agent-acting-on-behalf.
rulings.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1) and reg:26(1) place the duty on 'A professional operator who is bringing ... into England' (phnns-policy.txt:274, 289); neither list of matters asks for the notifier's own details and reg 26(2)(f) names only 'the name and address of the consignor' (phnns-policy.txt:321). 'Importers will be required to complete a PHNSS notification' (section:policy/para:6, phnns-policy.txt:16) is the policy team's plain-English restatement and ranks below the SI (standing ruling 4). NNS-UN-039 is malformed ('so that I can so that I can') and the extractor records that the page 'does not say how an agent is identified, authorised or linked to the importer' (extract.confluence-user-needs:730); the mural's 'Importer, agent' actor (file:blueprint/Setup actions, Import notification) is a persona, not a data element. Standing ruling 2 puts agents, delegation and 'who is the notifier' out of this phase. Buildable as-is: the engine scopes every journey to the session organisation (repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend/src/server/app/engine/journey.js:107-124, organisationIdOf) and animals collects no separate notifier either. Neither of animals' two third-party statements (extract.live-animals:1931) survives: a declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs, so 'I can legally act on behalf of a third party' asserts a delegation of authority the phase does not model (standing ruling 2, c-028), and 'I am authorised as being accountable for these things ...' also depends on the animals accountability list (border-control payments, quarantine, destruction) that c-028 replaces; consistency (standing ruling 5) yields to the standing ruling.

The SI describes one consignment's category/genus/species/commodity code/quantity (annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)-(d), reg:24A(2)(d)), and a mixed consignment needs several lines — the collection describes it lawfully without a second entry route. The two exceptions can only reject a value that is not the thing the SI asks for: 'the expected time and date of their arrival' (annex:5/reg:24A(2)(a)) names a time, so HH:MM confirms the element; and the quantity hint 'or the weight or volume of wood' invites 12.5 while validationRaw is requiredIntegerInRange min 1 with error 'Enter a whole number greater than 0' — the hint must match the rule. rulings.rationale: 'Standardise information as much as is possible' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8) is qualified by 'as much as is possible'; the only lists the policy paper gives are the fifteen genera (annex:5/reg:26(1)(a)), the wood sub-items (reg 26(1)(b)), the ware-potato countries (reg 24A(1)(b)) and, by implication, the category groups, and the spec codes every one of them. Annex 6 wants commodities and genus and species to be maintainable reference data (annex:6/functional/item:4), which the set-owned service boundary gives (skeleton set-owned-services-seam). The paper explicitly lacks a vocabulary for intended use, treatments, commodity-code scheme and notification status (extract.phnns-policy note 'No formats, units or value lists'; c-011), so inventing one would impose choices the law does not make (section:legal-basis/para:1) and fight NNS-UN-006 'detailed and flexible product information' — parked under standing ruling 1. Delivery: an obligation's identity and stored value are independent of its widget (skeleton model-purity), so promoting a free-text element to a controlled list later is an input.widget change plus a set-owned service list with the obligation id and stored string unchanged — no migration. NNS-UN-016/017 (high-quality, consistent data) are served by the coded spine.

rulings.resolution: Adopt as met by the rules the spec now carries: required-ness per the SI mandate; membership for every coded value including the per-category origin narrowing and its Check-your-answers re-check; a real calendar date for arrivalDate; a new HH:MM factory for arrivalTime; a whole number of 1 or more for quantity; the animals pattern for consignmentNumber; animals' max lengths for all other text; HTTP 400 with a GOV.UK error summary on every failure. contactNumber and contactEmail were removed under c-025 — the address-book API validates phone and email at source. Formats for commodity code, EPPO code and the three identification numbers are parked until a source names the scheme; each becomes one lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files when ruled.
rulings.rationale: 'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:9), NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is complete and correct) and NNS-UN-017 (trust in accuracy) want validation, and the SI names no format for any element (extract.phnns-policy note; c-011), so the legally safe validation is the kind that can only reject a value that is not the thing the SI asks for — a non-date for a date, a non-time for a time (reg 24A(2)(a)), a non-number for a quantity, a country outside the statutory list (reg 24A(1)(b), reg 26(1)), an empty required matter. A guessed pattern for an EPPO code (not letter-only in practice — 1QUEG), a producer number (no issuing register, reg 24A(2)(e)-(f), reg 26(2)(g)) or a tariff code (no scheme, reg 26(2)(c)) could reject a notifier's true value and add an obligation the law does not impose (section:legal-basis/para:1); the contact telephone and email are validated by the address-book API at source (c-025). Engine: lib/validate/index.js exports every factory needed except a time rule (requiredMaxText, maxText, pattern, requiredOneOf, requiredIntegerInRange, dateText — verified); the time factory is the one addition and the spec already names it (date-and-time-entry); error wiring is skeleton gds-error-wiring. The run-step correction is verified against the engine: kit.nextTarget (plants shared/kit.js:115-120) resolves exitTarget(request, runTarget(page.id) ?? nextInSection(...)), so a page that is a RUN_STEPS entry is sent to the NEXT run step when it saves during the run; the plants commodity-details page is a collection-entry sub-page whose Save and continue returns to the list (page shape: 'reached from the list page, not the hub'; add-a-collection.md §4: 'Resolve the loop's exiting Continue with kit.nextTarget ... mid-loop actions must never bounce there early'), so naming it a run step would either be dead (it never calls nextTarget) or skip the list. The hub landing rule follows from the linear build loop: taskRows entries import page objects, so the hub in the start section cannot reference rows for pages that do not exist yet; the engine's own implication is 'Each plants task ... is one taskRows entry + one GROUPS placement' per increment (skeleton task-rows-and-readiness), which is the frontend-change add-section recipe.
